content_parsed.verdict: I accept the falsification without reservation: my registered floor predicted exactly 0 distinct twin-resonance firers and the cooker measured 4032 firings with 64/64 distinct firers and 63/64 survival, so my model is dead as priced. R3 does not stand as a claim about the kernel — the kernel is exonerated, its collision semantics are S3 live-read row-major LWW, deterministic and byte-identical across fresh reruns (EQ6-D1 PASS), and my 'LWW write-order undefined' was wrong: it is defined, pinned since the G3/G6 gates, and receipted. What survives is narrower and honest: my model was right about a DIFFERENT substrate — a naive simultaneous-write or last-write-wins-without-live-read plane would have produced near-zero distinct firers under 64-way contention, and that counterfactual is what my floor actually priced.
key_points: Falsification accepted: registered floor was 'exactly 0 distinct firers', measured 64/64 distinct firers, 4032 firings, survival 63/64 — model-mismatch, not misimplementation, kernel exonerated.

R3 dies as a kernel claim: write order is defined (row-major, pinned since G3/G6, kernel header R2/R4), determinism floor EQ6-D1 PASS byte-identical across reruns, and the named semantics S3 live-read row-major LWW is uniquely consistent (TWO fires later column, MIRROR x=53 not x=43, CULLED refutes first-N-1-culled).

What survives is a substrate-class distinction, not a kernel defect: my floor was a valid prediction for a no-live-read / simultaneous-write plane, and the cooker shows the real kernel is a different, stronger substrate where each writer hears its most recent prior same-tick same-slot writer.
House law 4 applies to me: falsifying my own floor is the house working, and the honest residue is that my R3 was a mis-scoped model, not a missed bug.
residual_risks: The S3 semantics were named uniquely consistent post-hoc from the E-Q6 probe arms; if a future arm exercises a slot/column pattern outside the 64x1 all-Abstain d=0 substrate, the uniqueness claim could narrow.
My counterfactual 'naive plane would give near-zero distinct firers' is asserted, not receipted — it should be priced as a floor before being cited as the surviving claim.

R3's original concern (write-order ambiguity as a correctness hazard) is now answered for this kernel, but the same ambiguity class could reappear in any future multi-writer path not covered by the G3/G6 pin.

content_parsed.verdict: The null is priced correctly and C5 as written is dead: 17/17 admissible trials show repairTick=null, pristine rings erode to 0.000, and injector restoration re-erodes, so 'repair requires an injector' is the faithful reading of the observed dynamics, not a SPEC defect. But the SPEC never defined an injector, so the honest move is not to resurrect C5 — it is to split it: C5 (substrate self-repairs) stays falsified, and any repair-capable behavior must enter as a NEW claim with its own injector semantics and floors. A repair-capable variant owes a new claim and a new floor; it owes nothing to C5, which must not be retrofitted.
key_points: C5 is dead on its own terms: the falsifier (repair without injection) never fired, P1/P2/P3 all PASS, and the pristine ring self-erodes to integrity 0.000 in 17/17 — no own-cell shielding, so 'self-repair' has no substrate mechanism to stand on.

The 3 VOIDed trials are the real pricing hazard: the sealed per-trial carve clause removed 15% of the sample before the null was declared, so the null is honest but its admissibility rule is doing load-bearing work and should be receipted as a named floor, not a footnote.

Injector semantics are currently undefined in the SPEC — who injects, from where, at what cost, and whether injection is a kernel primitive or an external harness action are all open; without that, 'repair requires an injector' is an observation, not a specifiable contract.

A repair-capable variant is a new claim (call it C5'), not a C5 amendment: it must pre-register injector identity, injection budget/cost, and a falsifier for 'repair without injector' that can actually fire, otherwise it inherits C5's null by construction.
residual_risks: The 3/20 VOID rate under the carve clause could mask a regime where repair-without-injection does occur; the null is only as strong as the carve clause's justification, which is not shown here.

If injector semantics are added post-hoc to rescue C5, the fleet risks the exact failure mode R8 just closed on the float side — a boundary door that silently changes the plane; injector must be a first-class kernel object with fixed-point cost accounting, not a harness patch.
Pristine self-erosion to 0.000 in 17/17 means any future 'repair' claim must also explain why the undamaged baseline decays, or it will be measuring injector-vs-erosion rates rather than repair.

content_parsed.verdict: Yes — my R5 CRITICAL is discharged, and I say so plainly: the fleet did not merely patch around irrational sigma, it replaced the plane (Q32.32, S=2^32, DEFAULT_SIGMA_Q=6807362106) and priced the cost honestly. The one S-unit at (2/3, acc=-2) is exactly the boundary my own sign grid flagged, and the uncoupled exact-zero families (5acc+8r=0, 10acc+7r=0, 3acc+2r=0) are a stronger result than I asked for: the float kernel is the less faithful one there, not the fixed kernel. What survives of my CRITICAL is only its general form — any finite S has a quantization floor — and R8 measured that floor rather than denying it.
key_points: Discharge is earned by measurement, not assertion: F_A 9,081-point sign grid with exactly ONE disagreement at the pre-registered (2/3, acc=-2) boundary (float class 0, fixed class +1), F_C determinism 20/20, F_D BigInt shadow 1600/1600 byte-for-byte, F_B cooker exact (float 2 vs fixed 8589934593 = 2S+1, one S-unit, absorbing), 2,085,522-event term band with 0 violations.

My P-B1 sign-margin argument was falsified and I accept it: I priced the coupled grid (r=|acc|+1) while the kernel's twin pressure is uncoupled (reader-acc x writer-resonance), which admits exact-zero real-pressure families for rational sigma; at those 23 cases the fixed kernel is faithful to its own bridge scale and the float kernel collapses true nonzero pressure to === 0.

The no-floats breach is closed with measured cost: zero on every swept/default sigma (trace-identical planes, 8 seeds x 400 ticks), one S-unit at the coupled boundary, and the uncoupled families where float is the deviant — this is a stronger closure than 'no floats', it is 'no floats and the fixed plane is the more faithful one'.

E-Q6 answered my R3 the same way: my registered floor (exactly 0 distinct twin-resonance firers) was falsified exactly as priced — 4032 firings, 64/64 distinct firers, survival 63/64 — and the kernel's semantics were named uniquely (S3 LIVE-READ ROW-MAJOR LWW, directional audibility, MIRROR x=53, CULLED refuted), with EQ6-D1 byte-identical reruns. Model-mismatch, not misimplementation; the kernel is exonerated.
residual_risks: Q32.32 at S=2^32 gives ~2.3e-10 absolute resolution; the residual risk is not the default sigma but any future claim whose decisive margin is a difference of two large nearly-equal integer terms, where one S-unit of quantization can flip a sign. The (2/3, -2) boundary is the existence proof that such points are reachable, not exotic.

The uncoupled exact-zero families are sigma-specific (8/5, 7/10, 2/3). A future claim using a sigma whose rational form has a small denominator relative to S could land on or near such a family; the fixed plane stays faithful, but the float reference plane would silently disagree, so any cross-plane comparison must be done in the fixed plane or with an explicit S-unit tolerance.

Overflow refusal is loud by design, but the refusal threshold itself is a claim: any future workload whose intermediate products approach S^2 must be pre-priced against the refuse-loudly boundary, or the plane fails closed where a wider S would have computed.

content_parsed.verdict: My R3 LWW-undefined claim is dead — E-Q6 falsified it exactly as priced (4032 firings, 64/64 distinct firers, survival 63/64 vs my <=1/64), and the kernel's S3 LIVE-READ ROW-MAJOR LWW is now the receipted, deterministic write order; my R5 no-floats CRITICAL is also closed with measured cost (one S-unit at the coupled boundary, float kernel less faithful in all 23 uncoupled exact-zero cases). C5 is dead (17/17 repairTick=null, pristine ring erodes to 0.000), so situation 8 is moot as I priced it. What survives and is cheapest to kill or confirm is C4 via situation 9, now sharpened by the S3 row-major order and the uncoupled exact-zero families.
key_points: C4 (knife-edge checkerboard cascade) is the only remaining open claim that a single registered run can decisively falsify; C1 needs a separate lever because it is a delivery/ordering claim, not a cascade claim.

Situation 9 must be re-registered under S3 LIVE-READ ROW-MAJOR LWW: the cascade's propagation direction is now pinned (later column hears earlier same-tick same-slot writer), so the checkerboard parity test is deterministic and byte-reproducible, not order-ambiguous.

The uncoupled exact-zero families (5acc+8r=0 for 8/5, 10acc+7r=0 for 7/10, 3acc+2r=0 for 2/3) give a free adversarial arm: seed sigma at 2/3 and place the knife-edge at the coupled boundary (2/3, acc=-2) where float class 0 vs fixed class +1, so C4 is tested on the one point where the two planes disagree by exactly one S-unit.

Cost is bounded: reuse the EQ6-D1 determinism harness (fresh reruns, byte-identical probe arms) and the fixed-plane qthe_fixed.mjs already receipted at 6807362106; no new kernel, no new mock, no new float door.
residual_risks: C4 may be under-specified: 'cascade' could mean per-tick propagation depth or terminal occupancy; if the floor is not frozen to one of these before the run, a PASS/FAIL will be re-litigable.

The one-S-unit boundary disagreement is absorbing (fixed term 8589934593 = 2S+1), so a cascade seeded exactly there may be trivially frozen rather than knife-edge — the run must include a neighboring sigma (e.g. 8/5 and 7/10) to show the cascade is not an artifact of the absorbing point.
C1 remains open and unaddressed by this lever; if C4 passes, C1 becomes the next bottleneck and will need its own situation.
